### The sealed note

#### I.

<!--index:
archive~
sealed note
cases \\ missing ledger~
-->

Mira arrived just before dusk, carrying a notebook, a folded map, and the kind
of expression that suggested she had already solved half the mystery.

"You are late," Rowan said.

"Only by the clock," Mira replied. "By the story, I am right on time."

The room held a writing desk, two lamps, and a stack of envelopes tied with
green thread. One of those envelopes had been opened and closed so often that
its seal had become a pale circle rather than a mark of wax.

<!-- index:
schedule
weather \\ rain
objects \\ envelopes
-->

Outside, rain tapped against the window in a slow, even pattern. Inside, Rowan
spread the map flat and traced a route from the harbor to the old records hall.
The ink had run in one corner, but the street names were still readable.

> "We do not need a dramatic theory," Mira said.
>
> "We need a plain one that survives contact with facts."

That answer settled the matter for a moment. Rowan lit the second lamp and
placed the sealed note between them. The paper was thick, the handwriting
careful, and the signature missing entirely.

<!-- index:
cases \\ old tower
cases \\ sealed note \\ signature~
-->

The message itself was brief:

"Come alone. Bring the ledger. Use the west stair. Do not trust the bell."

No one in the room said anything after that. The instructions were too precise
to be random and too strange to be routine.

### II.

By midnight they had agreed on a plan:

1. Check the records hall before dawn.
2. Copy the ledger pages instead of moving the original.
3. Leave a reply in the empty brass mailbox behind the tower.

If the note was a trap, they would learn who expected an answer. If it was not,
they would still know why someone had gone to such trouble to stay unnamed.
